original_question: The Gruenberg–Kegel graph(or the prime graph) GK(G) of a finite group G is a labelled graph with vertex set consisting of all prime divisors of the order of G in which different vertices p and q are adjacent if and only if G contains an element of order pq. Let GK(G) denote the abstract graph obtained from GK(G) by removing all labels. A finite group G is said to be recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph if there are no finite groups H not isomorphic to G with GK(H) isomorphic to GK(G). Are there infinitely many(pairwise non-isomorphic) finite groups which are recognizable by the isomorphism type of the Gruenberg–Kegel graph?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.94 (N. V. Maslova) in the New Problems section of the 21st issue: "Are there infinitely many (pairwise non-isomorphic) finite groups which are recognizable by the isomorphism type of the Gruenberg–Kegel graph?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation. It correctly defines the labelled Gruenberg–Kegel graph using prime divisors of |G| and adjacency via existence of an element of order pq; it then switches to the underlying unlabeled abstract graph; it defines recognizability by isomorphism type of that abstract graph rather than by equality of labelled graphs; and it asks exactly the same existence question about infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups.
missing_details: The only real issue is notational clarity: the draft reuses GK(G) both for the labelled prime graph and for its underlying unlabeled abstract graph. For a fully stand-alone formulation faithful to the paper’s intent, these should be distinguished explicitly by words or by separate notation.
refined_question: Let GK(G) be the labelled Gruenberg–Kegel graph of a finite group G: its vertices are the prime divisors of |G|, and two distinct primes p and q are adjacent if and only if G contains an element of order pq. Let the underlying unlabeled abstract graph of GK(G) be obtained by forgetting the prime labels. Say that G is recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph if, whenever H is a finite group whose underlying unlabeled Gruenberg–Kegel graph is isomorphic to that of G, one has H ≅ G. Are there infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups G with this property?
justification: This draft is targeting the paper’s exact open problem 21.94, essentially word for word, rather than an older neighboring problem about groups with the same labelled prime graph. In this paper, the problem is posed specifically for recognizability by the isomorphism type of the unlabeled Gruenberg–Kegel graph, not for recognizability by the labelled graph itself. The only nearby contextual addition in the paper is the note after Problem 21.95, which observes that recognizability by isomorphism type implies recognizability by the Gruenberg–Kegel graph and hence almost simplicity; that consequence is context, not part of the question itself.
